pack.description: Vocabulary of linguistics passages and talks: sounds, grammar, meaning and language change.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory linguistics texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: the rules for how words are put together to form sentences
entries.example_academic: Children master the basic syntax of their language without explicit instruction.
entries.example_spoken: My vocabulary is fine; it's the syntax that trips me up.

entries.definition: a form of a language that is spoken in one area or by one group, with its own words and grammar
entries.example_academic: The northern dialect preserves verb forms that disappeared elsewhere.
entries.example_spoken: My grandparents speak a dialect I can barely follow.

entries.definition: relating to the sounds of speech
entries.example_academic: A phonetic transcription records what was actually said, not how it is spelled.
entries.example_spoken: English spelling isn't phonetic at all.

entries.definition: relating to the meaning of words and sentences
entries.example_academic: The two words overlap in form but have no semantic connection.
entries.example_spoken: That's just a semantic difference; we agree on the facts.

entries.definition: able to speak two languages well, or using two languages
entries.example_academic: Bilingual children switch languages according to the person they are addressing.
entries.example_spoken: She's bilingual, so she takes notes in both languages.

entries.definition: the ability to speak or write a language easily, smoothly and without many pauses
entries.example_academic: Fluency develops through sustained practice rather than through grammar study alone.
entries.example_spoken: My fluency improved a lot after the exchange year.

entries.definition: a speech sound made with the mouth open and the air flowing freely, such as the sounds written a, e, i, o, u
entries.example_academic: The language distinguishes long vowels from short ones.
entries.example_spoken: French has nasal vowels that English doesn't have.

entries.definition: a speech sound made by partly or completely stopping the flow of air, such as b, k or s
entries.example_academic: Clusters of three consonants are difficult for speakers of many languages.
entries.example_spoken: He drops the final consonant in a lot of words.

entries.definition: the process of learning a language or skill, or of getting something
entries.example_academic: Second-language acquisition is influenced by age, motivation and exposure.
entries.example_spoken: Her research is on language acquisition in toddlers.

entries.definition: the rise and fall of the voice when speaking
entries.example_academic: Rising intonation can turn a statement into a question without any change in word order.
entries.example_spoken: Your grammar was fine, but the intonation sounded angry.

entries.definition: a unit of sound in a word, usually containing one vowel sound
entries.example_academic: In English, an unstressed syllable is often reduced to a weak central vowel.
entries.example_spoken: Which syllable do you stress in that word?

entries.definition: a word taken from one language and used in another
entries.example_academic: Loanwords reveal which cultures a community traded with.
entries.example_spoken: That's a loanword from Japanese.

entries.definition: a letter or group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning
entries.example_academic: The prefix reverses the meaning of the adjective to which it is attached.
entries.example_spoken: Just add the prefix and you get the opposite.

entries.definition: a person who has spoken a particular language since early childhood
entries.example_academic: Even native speakers disagree about whether the sentence is acceptable.
entries.example_spoken: I asked a native speaker to check my email.

entries.definition: the first language that a person learns as a child at home
entries.example_academic: Instruction in the mother tongue improves literacy in the early years of school.
entries.example_spoken: Arabic is her mother tongue, but she studied in French.

entries.definition: relating to language or to the scientific study of language
entries.example_academic: Linguistic diversity is declining as small communities shift to major languages.
entries.example_spoken: There's a linguistic barrier between the two teams.

entries.definition: the study of how words are formed from smaller parts, or the form and structure of living things
entries.example_academic: The morphology of the verb marks both the tense and the person of the subject.
entries.example_spoken: Turkish morphology is fascinating: one word can be a whole sentence.

entries.definition: the smallest unit of sound in a language that can make one word different from another
entries.example_academic: English treats the two sounds as separate phonemes, whereas Spanish does not.
entries.example_spoken: Those two words differ by just one phoneme.

entries.definition: all the words of a language, or all the words that a person or group knows
entries.example_academic: The lexicon of the language was enriched by centuries of contact with traders.
entries.example_spoken: Half of my lexicon in English comes from TV shows.

entries.definition: the study of how context and the speaker's intention affect the meaning of what is said
entries.example_academic: Pragmatics explains why "Can you pass the salt?" is not a question about ability.
entries.example_spoken: Understanding sarcasm is all about pragmatics.

entries.definition: the origin and history of a word, or the study of this
entries.example_academic: The etymology of the place name points to an earlier, vanished population.
entries.example_spoken: I looked up the etymology, and the word comes from Arabic.

entries.definition: a simple form of language that develops so that groups without a shared language can talk to each other
entries.example_academic: A pidgin has a reduced grammar and is nobody's first language.
entries.example_spoken: The traders communicated in a pidgin based on Portuguese.

entries.definition: a full language that has developed from a mixture of languages and is spoken as a first language by a community
entries.example_academic: Once children acquire it as a first language, the pidgin develops into a creole.
entries.example_spoken: Haitian creole is the language most people speak at home there.

entries.definition: a word that has the same origin as a word in another language
entries.example_academic: Cognates make reading easier for learners whose first language is related.
entries.example_spoken: "Night" and the German "Nacht" are cognates.

entries.definition: a change in the form of a word, often its ending, that shows its grammatical role
entries.example_academic: English has lost most of the inflections that once marked case.
entries.example_spoken: Latin has an inflection for almost everything.

entries.definition: a language used for communication between groups of people who speak different first languages
entries.example_academic: Latin served as the lingua franca of European scholarship for centuries.
entries.example_spoken: English is the lingua franca in our lab.

entries.definition: a sound made by gliding from one vowel to another within the same syllable
entries.example_academic: The diphthong in "house" was a simple long vowel in earlier English.
entries.example_spoken: Spanish speakers sometimes turn that vowel into a diphthong.

entries.definition: the patterns of stress, rhythm and tone in speech
entries.example_academic: Infants respond to the prosody of their native language before they understand words.
entries.example_spoken: Her prosody is so natural that people think she grew up here.

entries.definition: the practice of changing from one language or variety to another in the same conversation
entries.example_academic: Code-switching follows grammatical rules and signals group membership.
entries.example_spoken: There's a lot of code-switching at home; we mix Spanish and English.
